en-US.longDescription: RelayPony for the desktop sends and receives files between your computer and your phones, encrypted end to end with the age protocol. Pairs by QR code with the RelayPony iOS and Android apps. No server, no cloud, no account.
en-US.name: RelayPony
en-US.releaseNotes:
RelayPony Desktop 4.0.0 catches the desktop app up with RelayPony 4 on Android and iPhone: same pairing, same protocol, same layout.
What's new
- Pair with a QR code or a short word code, both ways at once. Word codes use the same Rust core as the phones (RelayPonyPake).
- Only paired devices can send to you, unless you allow others in Advanced.
- Send over the internet when the other device isn't on your network. It tries a direct connection first and falls back to the relay, encrypted end to end either way.
- Send folders and text. Received lists everything that arrived, with Open and Open folder, and Copy for text and links.
- Unpairing tells the other device.
- New layout: Send and Received in the sidebar, with Settings and Advanced behind the app bar.
- Seven languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), German, French, Japanese and Hindi. Switch in Settings without restarting.
- Dark theme (#1). Settings has System default, Light and Dark, and on Linux System default now follows your desktop's setting.
Command line
- relaypony pair --words shows a word code for the other device to type. relaypony pair --word-code <code> pairs with one.
- relaypony relay-check tests every relay call internet transfers make, from this computer.
Upgrading
Your identity and pairings carry over. A device still on RelayPony 3 can pair with the older QR code: in the pair dialog, pick "Other device on RelayPony 3? Show the older code".
Building from source
The protocol core now comes from RelayPonyAndroid as a submodule, and word codes need a Rust toolchain. Clone with --recurse-submodules and see the README.
